text:
Mikel Arteta speaks to Amazon Prime. “[A top-eight finish in the league phase] is what we want … [Borussia Dortmund] are a top, top side … we are going to have to be really good to beat them today … we want to kill the games … to put them to bed early … this season has been a lot of victories by small margins … those margins in my opinion should be bigger.”
He also reports that David Raya is on the mend, but is careful to make no promises of a return at the weekend against Manchester City. “We need some more tests … he is evolving well … we have to wait and see.”
Borussia Dortmund name future England international Jobe Bellingham in their midfield. Jude’s brother, formerly of Birmingham City and Sunderland, isn’t the only ex-Premier League player in their starting XI: Fábio Silva, once of Wolverhampton Wanderers (and Rangers), leads the line. Germany midfielder Felix Nmecha played a couple of games for Manchester City, but not in the league. All of which leaves the outrageously talented 19-year-old Greece winger Konstantinos Karetsas on the bench. Scotland supporters are permitted to let one ice-cold bead of sweat roll down their spinal cord.
Arsenal make six changes to their starting XI following the 2-2 draw at Newcastle United. One is enforced: David Raya is injured, so up steps Kepa. Meanwhile in come Ben White, Piero Hincapié, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyökeres. Jurriën Timber, Eberechi Eze, Riccardo Calafiori, Kai Havertz and Bruno Guimarães drop to the bench.
Arsenal: Kepa, White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis, Gyokeres.
Subs: Meslier, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman, Porter.
Borussia Dortmund: Kobel, Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Ryerson, Nmecha, Veerman, Svensson, Bellingham, Beier, Silva.
Subs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Duarte, Reggiani.
The champions and runaway leaders of the Premier League meet the leaders of the Bundesliga. That’s quite a sexy sell, even if it’s almost totally Jeopardy Lite™ (the official caveat of the Uefa Champions League Swiss System). Arsenal are on a roll, having won their last 12 group/league phase matches in a row; if they make it 13 tonight, they’ll equal an English record currently held by Liverpool. Dortmund meanwhile are unbeaten this season in the league, and are three wins from four in Europe. Throw in the fact that none of Arsenal’s 46 games against German teams have ended goalless, something that can also be said of BVB’s last 58 away matches in the Champions League, and we could be onto something here. Kick-off round Ashburton Grove way is at 8pm GMT. It’s on!
digest_he:
שתי קבוצות צמרת נפגשות למשחק מרתק במסגרת ליגת האלופות, כאשר ארסנל פוגשת את בורוסיה דורטמונד באצטדיון האשברטון גרוב. המאמן מיקל ארטטה נאלץ לבצע שינויים בהרכב הפותח, ביניהם הצבתו של קפה בשער בשל פציעתו של דויד ראיה, לצד שחקנים כמו בן ווייט וויקטור גיוקרס.

מן העבר השני, בורוסיה דורטמונד מגיעה להרכב הכולל שחקנים מוכרים ומבטיחים, במטרה לשמור על רצף התוצאות הטובות שלה באירופה. המפגש בין מוליכת הפרמייר ליג למובילת הבונדסליגה מבטיח כדורגל איכותי וקצבי.
